Diagnostics of extracted trends

Source: R/trend_index.R
trend_diagnostics.Rd

Summarises, per key, how much of the movement of the seasonally adjusted series the trend absorbs, how smooth it is and whether the remainder still has autocorrelation or exceeds the sampling-noise floor.

Usage

trend_diagnostics(tr, key_cols, n_col = NULL, time_col = NULL)

Arguments

tr

Output of extract_trend() (possibly with an added column of counts).

key_cols

Character vector of key columns.

n_col

Name of a column of counts in tr (number of postings for totals, denominator for shares), or NULL.

time_col

Name of the time column; by default taken from the time_col attribute of tr.

Value

A data.table with one row per key (and method, when present) and columns n_obs, ratio_trend_remainder, var_removed_d1, var_removed_d13, lb_p_value, roughness, remainder_var and, when n_col is given, noise_floor and ratio_floor.

Details

On each key, ordered by time:

  • ratio_trend_remainder: var(diff(trend)) / var(diff(remainder)).

  • var_removed_d1, var_removed_d13: share of the variance of the 1-week and 13-week differences of the seasonally adjusted series (observed - seasonal) removed by the trend, 1 - var(diff_h(remainder)) / var(diff_h(observed - seasonal)). The seasonally adjusted series is used because the seasonal component, not the trend, accounts for the 13-week movement of the raw series.

  • lb_p_value: Ljung-Box p-value of the remainder at lag 13.

  • roughness: variance of the second differences of the trend.

  • remainder_var: variance of the remainder.

  • When n_col is given: noise_floor and ratio_floor = remainder_var / noise_floor. For transform = "log" the floor is the Poisson variance of a log count, 1 / mean(n); for "logit" it is the binomial variance of a logit share, 1 / mean(n p (1 - p)) with p the observed share and n the denominator; for "none" it is NA. A ratio near 1 means the remainder is close to pure sampling noise.

Examples

set.seed(1)
weeks <- data.table::as.IDate("2023-05-01") + 7L * (0:155)
d <- data.table::data.table(
  source = "a",
  week = weeks,
  n = stats::rpois(156, exp(5 + 0.003 * seq_along(weeks)))
)
tr <- extract_trend(d, "source", "week", "n", harmonics = 1L)
tr[d, n := i.n, on = c("source", "week")]
